# luna — command reference (pinned v1.44.0) {#tools_luna}

<!-- GENERATED by devtools/gen_luna_doc.py from `luna --help`; do not edit.
     Regenerate after a pin bump: python3 devtools/gen_luna_doc.py -->

luna is the cycle-accurate emulator every OpenSNES test runs on
(`.claude/rules/testing.md`). The SDK pins one release in
`testing/luna.version`; `scripts/install-luna.sh` fetches it and
`make tests` uses nothing else. This page is that release's own `--help`,
one section per subcommand, so what you read here is what the pinned
binary accepts — not a newer or older luna.

How the SDK uses it: `luna run` for corpus liveness and visual hashes,
`luna state --assert` for the runtime ROMs and probes, `luna test` for
the `testing/manifests/*.toml`, `luna diff` for the Class A A/B,
`luna profile` for measured coverage and the cycle budget, `luna
wram-trace` behind the WRAM oracle. The MCP server (`luna mcp`) is the
interactive debugger (`docs/tutorials/debugging.md`).


## `luna --help`

```text
SNES emulator with introspection API

Usage: luna <COMMAND>

Commands:
  run          Load a ROM, step the CPU N instructions, optionally dump a screenshot of the resulting PPU state
  test         Run manifest-driven homebrew tests: one TOML per test (rom, input, run bound, asserts), executed in-process through `luna-api`. Exit 0 = all pass, 1 = assert failures, 2 = manifest/usage errors — the CI contract. The machine is set per manifest, not by flags: `region = "pal"` (or `"ntsc"`) forces the video standard as `--force-region` does, `force_mapper` the mapper, `power_on` / `seed` the RAM the ROM boots on
  mcp          Serve the Luna MCP server on stdio
  state        Run the emulator through `luna-api` and emit a JSON state snapshot — the same data the MCP `state` tool returns
  frames       Capture a sequence of EXACTLY-consecutive PPU frames as PNGs in one run, via the same `luna-api` render path the GUI uses. Use this to diagnose *temporal* artefacts (flicker / double-buffer page-flip desync) that a single `state --screenshot` cannot show — it samples one frame, so a frame-to-frame "blink" is invisible to it. Each frame's PNG is tagged with its frame number and the INIDISP forced-blank flag, so you can see exactly what the GUI would (and would not) display
  record       Record a run as a small video, a text timeline and contact sheets: `<OUT>.mp4` (H.264 + AAC, the picture at twice its size with a strip under it naming the frame, the time and the buttons held), `<OUT>.md` (when the picture moves, holds or goes off, when the pad changes, the sound second by second) and `<OUT>-1.png` … (one labelled picture per second). The video is for eyes and for the models that take one; the text and the sheets are for the ones that do not. The video needs `ffmpeg` on the machine; `--no-video` writes the rest without it. Exit 0 = written, 1 = the run or the encoder failed, 2 = usage error
  diff         Compare two ROMs frame by frame: run both in one process, hash the displayed frame at every PPU frame, and print MATCH / DIFF for each requested frame — MATCH when A's frame `F` equals B's frame at some `F ± tolerance` (the boot-length offset a codegen change can introduce). The "compare at equal frame" protocol that validates a compiler / library change. Exit 0 = all match, 1 = any DIFF, 2 = usage error
  profile      Real master cycles per symbol: every step credits its cycles — bus + internal cycles plus the DMA / HDMA / refresh stalls charged during it — to the instruction's address; the report folds those onto the nearest `.sym` label (or a 256-byte page without one), heaviest first. Replaces static instruction weights with what the machine paid
  ticks        Record named memory zones at every tick of a game, as JSONL in the `tick-record` format (version 1): a header line, one line per tick, and an end line a complete record always has. A tick is an arrival on a routine the spec names, read just before its first instruction, so two runs line up tick by tick whatever their speed — two builds of a game, or a port and the program it reproduces, recorded by another emulator in the same format. The zones are raw bytes in memory order; the header gives the byte order. Exit 0 = the record is complete, 1 = the run fell short of it (the end line says why), 2 = the spec was refused and nothing ran
  wram-trace   Emit per-frame (vblank-aligned) WRAM page hashes for a confound-free cross-emulator differential. Each line is `<ppu_frame> <h0> <h1> ... <hN>` where each `h` is the FNV-1a hash of one WRAM page (`--page-size` bytes, default 4 KiB → 32 pages). Because WRAM-at-vblank-N is the SAME game-frame in both luna and a reference emulator (no input ⟹ game logic advances once per NMI), the first frame whose page hash differs from the reference pins the first REAL state divergence — unlike scene- level windows the boot-frame offset confounds
  bench        Run every ROM in a directory headless, detect anomalies (crashes, freezes, dead APU, missing firmware), and write a compatibility report + one markdown bug file per finding. Stresses the CLI/API across the whole corpus. Reports stay local (under `--out`)
  race-sweep   Search the interrupt races of a routine: force an NMI (or an IRQ) before EACH instruction of `--from`..`--to`, from one snapshot, and compare the outcome with the run that was not interrupted. Warm up (`--warm-until-pc` / `--warm-frames`), snapshot, run the baseline to the end condition (`--until-pc` / `--until-frame`), read the `--compare` bytes, then for every instruction address of the range the baseline executed: restore, interrupt there, run to the same end, compare. A trial is identical, DIFFERS (the bytes are listed), NOT TAKEN (injection refused: NMITIMEN.7 clear, I flag set; never a pass) or END NOT REACHED (a hang, a lost wake-up). The injected edge is synthetic, as for `--inject-nmi-at`. Deterministic: the report is the same for any `--jobs`. The window must hold no interrupt of its own (a natural NMI): the baseline counts them and the sweep is refused unless `--allow-baseline-interrupt` (then NESTED trials)
  audio-check  Audio fault analyzer: find a gap (a hole in a sound that was playing), a click (a jump out of the slope of the signal), saturation (clipped runs) and, with --voices-dir, a voice cut (a voice that falls to silence with no release decay) in a WAV written by `luna state --audio-out` (and `--voice-wav-dir`). One line per fault (kind, frame, time, measured numbers, threshold name), or --json (schema 1). Frames are nominal: a WAV has no frame marks. It reads the core's stream, not the host's resampling or pacing
  cart-check   Audit a ROM's header for a physical cartridge (repro board / flash): copier header, checksum, sizes, map byte, vectors, SRAM and chipset, country, title. One line per finding, `SEVERITY CODE: message`
  strict       Hardware strict mode: run a ROM and list what a real console would have refused or corrupted — a VRAM/OAM/CGRAM write or a PPU memory read while the picture is drawn (R1-R4), a DMA through the blocked A-bus zone (R5) or between WRAM and $2180 (R6), a manual joypad read during the auto-read (R8), or of `$4218-$421F` (R9), a write to `$2100` with bit 7 on the data bus (R10) or to `$2133` over a different bus byte (R11) while the picture is drawn, brightness 0 with the display on over a lit picture for a whole frame (R12, an advisory: a console shows it faintly, luna draws black). It also checks, once a frame, the sprite tiles the picture draws: a tile with pixels that no write ever filled (S1, its content is the power-on VRAM) or that was uploaded under another OBSEL layout (S4). The journal only observes: the run is identical to a plain one. One line per distinct (rule, pc, address), one per distinct (S1/S4, tile)
  spc-dump     Run a ROM until its music driver is playing, then export the APU state as a `.spc` sound file (SNES-SPC700 Sound File Data v0.30): SPC700 registers + 64 KB ARAM + DSP registers + IPL ROM, playable in any SPC player. Step far enough in (and pulse Start via `--input`) that the music has started before the snapshot
  assets-dump  Run a ROM to a scene, then dump every graphics asset currently loaded as PNGs: the VRAM tile sheet, the four BG tilemaps, the CGRAM palette, the OAM sprite sheet, and the composited screen — plus raw `vram.bin` / `cgram.bin` and `oam.json`. This captures the assets *loaded at this instant* (already decompressed by the game); snapshot several scenes (via `--input` / different `-n`) to cover a whole game. A static whole-ROM rip is NOT possible — SNES graphics are game-specific-compressed with no standard layout
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version
```


## `luna run`

```text
Load a ROM, step the CPU N instructions, optionally dump a screenshot of the resulting PPU state.

A panic inside the core is caught and reported — the state reached so far is still dumped.

Usage: luna run [OPTIONS] <ROM>

Arguments:
  <ROM>
          Path to the .sfc / .smc ROM file

Options:
  -n, --steps <STEPS>
          Maximum number of CPU instructions to execute before dumping
          
          [default: 64]

      --until-frame <UNTIL_FRAME>
          Run until PPU frame N (then dump), instead of stopping at the `-n` instruction count — same as `state --until-frame`. Pins a `--print-fbhash` / `--screenshot` baseline to a PPU frame so a codegen change that shifts the instruction count cannot move the capture onto another animation phase

      --screenshot <SCREENSHOT>
          If set, render the composited framebuffer as a PNG and write it to the given path: 256×224, 256×239 while the game runs in overscan, or 512×448 (512×478 in overscan) with `--native-res`

      --force-display
          Bypass INIDISP forced-blank when rendering. Lets you see whatever the game has uploaded to VRAM/CGRAM even if its init left the screen blanked (e.g. a title still waiting on a Start press)

      --bg <BG>
          If set (1..=4), render ONLY that BG layer. Default is the composited BG3-over-BG1-over-BG2 frame (right for most Mode-1 title screens)

      --audio-out <AUDIO_OUT>
          If set, capture the APU's stereo 32 kHz output and write it to a WAV file at the end of the run. Lets the emulator be audio-verified without a GUI / sound card

      --nocash-out <NOCASH_OUT>
          If set, capture the program's `$21FC` Nocash-TTY output (the SDK's `SNES_NOCASH` / `SNES_ASSERT` debug channel) and write the raw byte stream to this file. Lets a headless harness read the ROM's own log / assertion output with no GUI debugger

      --wdm-out <WDM_OUT>
          If set, write captured `WDM $xx` executions (the SDK breakpoint / `SNES_ASSERT` channel — `WDM $00`) to this file, one `PC=$xxxxxx operand=$xx` line per hit. A non-empty file means an assertion or breakpoint fired during the run

      --print-fbhash
          If set, print a hash of the displayed frame (honouring `--force-display`) to stdout as `fbhash=<16-hex>`. A stable, cross-architecture visual-regression key — it hashes the same pixels `--screenshot` writes, before PNG encoding (so it is immune to the build-dependent PNG encoder). Ideal as an external test harness's baseline key. See `docs/trace_determinism.md` for which outputs (fbhash / trace counts / WRAM bytes) are cross-arch-stable and how strongly each may be asserted

      --native-res
          Emit the native 512×448 frame: hi-res modes 5/6 and pseudo-512 keep their two horizontal subpixels per dot, interlace keeps both fields as separate lines — instead of the default 256×224 averaged view. Applies to `--screenshot` and `--print-fbhash`

      --force-mapper <FORCE_MAPPER>
          Force a cartridge mapper, bypassing header auto-detection — same as `state`/`frames`. Needed for checksum-invalid homebrew / reference ROMs (e.g. the `PeterLemon` corpus) so they can reach `--print-fbhash`. One of: lorom, hirom, exhirom, sa1, superfx, dsp1, sdd1; spc7110 is recognised but not emulated, the load refuses it

      --force-region <FORCE_REGION>
          Force the video standard (ntsc, pal), overriding the cartridge header's country byte. Changes the scanline count (262/312) and frame rate — required to reproduce the golden harness, which runs the `PeterLemon` corpus as PAL to match krom's reference captures

      --power-on <POWER_ON>
          What RAM holds before the ROM boots: `zero` (default), `ones`, `random` (a seed is derived and printed) or `random=<seed>` (decimal or 0x hex — replays an exact machine). Fills WRAM, VRAM, CGRAM, OAM, APU RAM and the cartridge RAM no battery keeps (Game Pak RAM, BW-RAM, I-RAM); a boot bug that only shows on real hardware's garbage RAM shows here too

      --strict-hw
          Hardware strict mode: also journal what a real console would refuse or corrupt (see `luna strict`) and print it after the state. Exit 1 if there is any fault. Observation only: the run itself is unchanged

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```


## `luna test`

```text
Run manifest-driven homebrew tests: one TOML per test (rom, input, run bound, asserts), executed in-process through `luna-api`. Exit 0 = all pass, 1 = assert failures, 2 = manifest/usage errors — the CI contract. The machine is set per manifest, not by flags: `region = "pal"` (or `"ntsc"`) forces the video standard as `--force-region` does, `force_mapper` the mapper, `power_on` / `seed` the RAM the ROM boots on

Usage: luna test [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...  Manifest files, or directories scanned recursively for `*.toml`. Defaults to `./tests`

Options:
      --update           Rewrite each manifest's `asserts.fbhash`, the checkpoints' `fbhash` and the memory blocks that did not match with the measured values (regenerate goldens after an intended change). Formatting and comments are preserved
      --only <ONLY>      Only run manifests whose path contains this substring
      --report <REPORT>  Also print a machine-readable JSON report to stdout [possible values: json]
      --jobs <JOBS>      Run up to N manifests at once (0 = one per CPU). Each manifest gets its own emulator; the report is the same lines in the same order, and the same exit code, as a serial run. Manifests chained through a battery file (one's `srm_out` is another's `srm_in`) still run one after another, in path order; there is no other ordering between manifests [default: 1]
  -h, --help             Print help
```


## `luna mcp`

```text
Serve the Luna MCP server on stdio.

Once started, Luna exposes its full tool catalogue (load / run / observe / trace — see the book's MCP section, or the `capabilities` tool at runtime) to any connected MCP client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, custom clients). The process stays alive until the client closes the stream. With `--rom`, the session starts with the ROM (and symbols) already loaded.

Usage: luna mcp [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --rom <ROM>
          Preload a ROM so the client can skip `load_rom` (a `<rom>.sym` beside it is auto-loaded, wlalink-style)

      --sym <SYM>
          Explicit WLA-DX `.sym` to load after the ROM (overrides the beside-ROM auto-detection)

      --force-mapper <FORCE_MAPPER>
          Force the mapper for `--rom` instead of header auto-detection. One of: lorom, hirom, exhirom, sa1, superfx, dsp1, sdd1; spc7110 is recognised but not emulated, the load refuses it

      --force-region <FORCE_REGION>
          Force the video standard for `--rom` (ntsc, pal)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```


## `luna state`

```text
Run the emulator through `luna-api` and emit a JSON state snapshot — the same data the MCP `state` tool returns.

This is the dogfood path: the API surface that the CLI, GUI and MCP server all share. Use it to test the API directly without going through any transport.

Usage: luna state [OPTIONS] [ROM]

Arguments:
  [ROM]
          Path to the .sfc / .smc ROM file

Options:
      --schema
          Print the JSON Schema of the state JSON (`EmulatorState`, plus the `peeks` array `--out` adds) to stdout and exit — no ROM needed. The machine-readable map of every nested field a harness can `jq`

  -n, --steps <STEPS>
          CPU instructions to execute before snapshotting
          
          [default: 1000]

      --force-mapper <FORCE_MAPPER>
          Force a cartridge mapper, bypassing header auto-detection. Needed for headerless homebrew test ROMs (e.g. the `PeterLemon` Super FX / GSU plot tests). One of: lorom, hirom, exhirom, sa1, superfx, dsp1, sdd1; spc7110 is recognised but not emulated, the load refuses it

      --force-region <FORCE_REGION>
          Force the video standard (ntsc, pal), overriding the cartridge header's country byte. Changes the scanline count (262/312) and frame rate — required to reproduce the golden harness, which runs the `PeterLemon` corpus as PAL to match krom's reference captures

      --power-on <POWER_ON>
          What RAM holds before the ROM boots: `zero` (default), `ones`, `random` (a seed is derived and printed) or `random=<seed>` (decimal or 0x hex — replays an exact machine). Fills WRAM, VRAM, CGRAM, OAM, APU RAM and the cartridge RAM no battery keeps (Game Pak RAM, BW-RAM, I-RAM); a boot bug that only shows on real hardware's garbage RAM shows here too

      --dsp1-rom <DSP1_ROM>
          Install a DSP coprocessor firmware (`dsp1b.rom`) into luna's firmware folder, then load — needed for DSP-1 games (Super Mario Kart, Pilotwings). Persists for future runs

      --sym <SYM>
          Load a WLA-DX `.sym` symbol file (overrides the automatic `<rom>.sym` detection). Symbol names then annotate the CPU disassembly and resolve in the debug tooling

      --load-state <LOAD_STATE>
          Load a save state (a `.luna` blob from the GUI's save-state slots, `~/.local/luna/states/<rom-slug>.slot<N>.luna`) right after the ROM loads, before the `-n` warm-up. Lets a headless run resume from a GUI-captured scene (e.g. to inspect a bug the CLI can't reach without input). The state must match this ROM

      --wdm-out <WDM_OUT>
          Write captured `WDM $xx` executions (the SDK breakpoint / `SNES_ASSERT` channel) to this file — parity with `luna run`, so an input-driven test keeps the WDM oracle

      --print-fbhash
          Print `fbhash=<16-hex>` — the cross-arch-stable displayed-frame key (same as `luna run --print-fbhash`) — so an input-driven `state` run can also emit a visual baseline

      --call-stack
          Track the 65C816 call stack (JSR/JSL/RTS/RTL + interrupts) during the run; the `--out` JSON gains a `call_stack` array of `{pc, from, kind, symbol}` frames

      --native-res
          Emit the native 512×448 frame: hi-res modes 5/6 and pseudo-512 keep their two horizontal subpixels per dot, interlace keeps both fields as separate lines — instead of the default 256×224 averaged view. Applies to `--screenshot` and `--print-fbhash`

      --no-render
          Leave the picture uncomputed. The machine runs exactly the same (cycles, registers, VRAM / OAM / CGRAM, the `$213E` sprite flags) but no pixel is composed, about half the time of a run. For a run that reads memory and never the screen; refused with an option that reads the picture

      --layer-shots <LAYER_SHOTS>
          Write each layer of the last frame alone into this directory: `bg1.png` … `bg4.png`, `obj.png`, transparent where the layer shows nothing. Each is composed with the picture, line by line, so it is the same instant as `--screenshot`, HDMA and mid-frame writes included. A layer shows its own colour (before colour math, master brightness applied) wherever it reaches the main or the sub screen, TM / TS and their windows applied. The `--out` JSON gains `layers.overlaps`: every pair of layers that both show a pixel, with the count and the box around them

      --layers <LAYERS>
          With `--layer-shots`: only these layers, comma-separated (`bg1,bg2,bg3,bg4,obj`; default all five)

      --trace-log <TRACE_LOG>
          Mesen2's trace logger for the 65C816: one text row per instruction, written to PATH as Mesen2 writes its trace file — the 24-bit PC, two spaces, then the row as the format lays it out. The default format is Mesen2's (disassembly, effective address, value, registers, flags, scanline and dot)

      --trace-format <TRACE_FORMAT>
          With `--trace-log`: the row format, in Mesen2's tags (`[Disassembly]`, `[A,4h]`, `[Scanline,3]`, `[Align,38]`…; see the guide)

      --trace-condition <TRACE_CONDITION>
          With `--trace-log`: only the instructions for which this expression (the debugger's language) holds, at the opcode fetch or at one of the instruction's memory accesses

      --trace-no-labels
          With `--trace-log`: addresses as numbers, without the names of the labels and the loaded symbols (Mesen2's "Use labels" unticked)

      --dump-vram <DUMP_VRAM>
          Dump all 64 KB of PPU VRAM (raw bytes) to this file after the run. For diagnosing the framebuffer DMA → VRAM → display path

      --dump-coproc-ram <DUMP_COPROC_RAM>
          Dump the coprocessor work RAM (Super FX Game Pak RAM) raw bytes to this file, bypassing GSU ownership gating. For comparing luna's CPU-prepared GSU inputs against a reference

      --dump-aram <DUMP_ARAM>
          Dump all 64 KB of APU audio RAM (ARAM) raw bytes to this file. For diagnosing the SPC700 sound driver / CPU↔SPC handshake

      --out <OUT>
          Where to write the JSON state. Use `-` for stdout
          
          [default: -]

      --screenshot <SCREENSHOT>
          Optional screenshot output path (PNG)

      --screenshot-frames <A..B[/K]>
          Write one PNG per frame of a range into `--screenshot-dir`, in this one run: `A..B` is every frame from `A` to `B` included, `A..B/K` one frame in `K` from `A`. Each file is `frame_NNNNNN.png`, the picture `--until-frame N --screenshot` would write. Repeatable. Example: `--screenshot-frames 1090..1150/2 --screenshot-frames 1440..1560/3 --screenshot-dir shots --until-frame 1560`

      --screenshot-dir <SCREENSHOT_DIR>
          The directory `--screenshot-frames` writes into (created if absent)

      --vram-writers <PATH>
          Write who wrote what into VRAM over the run: one line per range of words and per source — the label a DMA read its bytes from, or the routine that wrote `$2118/$2119` — then the ranges two different sources both wrote. A tile sheet loaded over a tilemap shows there, where a frame hash only says the picture changed. The JSON report carries the same table (`vram_writers`)

      --vram-writers-from <FRAME>
          With `--vram-writers`: leave out the writes before this frame (the loading of the first screen)
          
          [default: 0]

      --audio-out <AUDIO_OUT>
          Optional audio dump path (32 kHz stereo WAV)

      --voice-wav-dir <VOICE_WAV_DIR>
          Also write each S-DSP voice on its own, `voice0.wav` to `voice7.wav` in this folder (created if absent): 32 kHz stereo, the voice's output after its envelope and its left / right volume, before the main volume, the echo and the `FLG` mute. Sample `n` of a file is sample `n` of `--audio-out`, so a note can be followed voice by voice. Sixty seconds unless `--voice-wav-seconds` says otherwise. Example: `--until-frame 1800 --voice-wav-dir voices/`

      --voice-wav-seconds <VOICE_WAV_SECONDS>
          With `--voice-wav-dir`: how many seconds of each voice to keep (default 60; each second costs about a megabyte of memory for the eight voices). A longer run says how many samples the files lack

      --input <INPUT>
          Scripted joypad-1 input. Format: comma-separated `frame:hex` checkpoints (frame number in decimal, hex mask with optional `0x` prefix). The mask is latched at the start of the named PPU frame and held until the next checkpoint overrides it.
          
          Example: `--input "100:0x1000,110:0"` holds Start (`$1000`) for frames 100..=109 then releases.
          
          JOY1 bit layout: B(15) Y(14) Sel(13) Start(12) Up/Down/Left/Right(11..8) A(7) X(6) L(5) R(4).

      --input2 <INPUT2>
          Scripted joypad-2 input, same `frame:hex` grammar as `--input` (a two-player probe, or replaying an MCP `script_p2` capture)

      --input3 <INPUT3>
          Scripted input for Super Multitap pads B, C, D — players 3, 4, 5 with `--port2 multitap` (pad A is player 2, `--input2`). Same grammar as `--input`

      --input4 <INPUT4>
          Player 4 (multitap pad C) — see `--input3`

      --input5 <INPUT5>
          Player 5 (multitap pad D) — see `--input3`

      --port1 <PORT1>
          Controller port-1 device: `pad` (default), `mouse`, `superscope`, `multitap`, or `none` for an unplugged port (its data lines read 0 for ever, where a pad's idle high — auto-read cannot tell them apart, only a manual read past bit 15 can)
          
          [default: pad]

      --port2 <PORT2>
          Controller port-2 device: `pad` (default), `mouse`, `superscope`, `multitap` (players 2-5: `--input2` … `--input5`), or `none` for an unplugged port — see `--port1`
          
          [default: pad]

      --mouse <MOUSE>
          Scripted SNES Mouse motion, applied to whichever port is set to `mouse`. `frame:dx,dy,buttons` entries separated by `;` (signed dx/dy; buttons bit0=left, bit1=right). Example: `--mouse "60:5,-3,1"`

      --superscope <SUPERSCOPE>
          Scripted Super Scope aim, applied to whichever port is set to `superscope`. `frame:x,y,buttons` entries separated by `;` (absolute screen pixels; buttons bit0=trigger, bit1=cursor, bit2=turbo, bit3=pause). Example: `--superscope "120:128,112,1"`

      --peek <PEEK>
          Optional memory peek(s) after snapshot.  Format: `BANK:OFFSET:COUNT` (ALL hex — `:20` is 32 bytes; a count can say its base, `:0x20` hex or `:#32` decimal), or a WLA-DX label `NAME[:COUNT]` resolved through the loaded `.sym` table (auto-detected `<rom>.sym` or `--sym`; count defaults to 1).  Can be specified multiple times.  The whole 24-bit space is readable (WRAM, ROM incl. `$C0-$FF` `HiROM`, SRAM, coproc RAM); the `$2000-$5FFF` register band reads `0` (no side effects), except the DMA registers `$4300-$437F` which read their real values, and an unmapped range reads `$FF` with a stderr note and `unmapped` in the JSON entry.  Output goes to stderr as a labelled hex dump.  Examples: `--peek 7E:0200:220`, `--peek monster_x:2`. `APU:OFFSET:COUNT` reads the SPC700's RAM, and `VRAM:WORD:COUNT` reads `COUNT` bytes of PPU VRAM from a **word** address (as `VMADD` takes it): `--peek VRAM:7340:6` is three tilemap entries. `CGRAM:COLOR:COUNT` reads `COUNT` bytes of the palette from a colour index (as `CGADD` takes it): `--peek CGRAM:10:#32` is the sixteen colours of palette 1. `OAM:OFFSET:COUNT` reads the PPU's own OAM (544 bytes, offset in hex; not the WRAM mirror): `--peek OAM:0:#16` is the first four sprites. `PPU:REGISTER:COUNT` reads `COUNT` write-only PPU registers as the PPU holds them: `--peek PPU:2101:1` is OBSEL (INIDISP, OBSEL, BGMODE, MOSAIC, M7SEL, `$2123-$212F`, CGWSEL, CGADSUB, SETINI; any other is refused)

      --assert <ASSERT>
          Assert memory equals expected bytes after warm-up. Format: `BANK:OFFSET=HEX` (all hex), or a WLA-DX label `NAME=HEX` resolved through the loaded `.sym` table. Prints `PASS`/`FAIL` per spec and exits non-zero if any fails. Repeatable. Examples: `--assert 7E:0010=AB12`, `--assert r_done=EFBE`

      --assert-aram <ASSERT_ARAM>
          Assert APU-RAM equals expected bytes (`OFFSET=HEX`). Like `--assert` but over ARAM. Repeatable

      --assert-vram <ASSERT_VRAM>
          Assert VRAM equals expected bytes (`OFFSET=HEX`). Like `--assert` but over VRAM. Repeatable

      --assert-cgram <ASSERT_CGRAM>
          Assert CGRAM (palette) equals expected bytes (`OFFSET=HEX`, byte offset into the 512-byte CGRAM, low byte of each colour first). Like `--assert` but over CGRAM. Repeatable

      --until-frame <UNTIL_FRAME>
          Run until PPU frame N (then snapshot), instead of stopping at the `-n` instruction count. Makes input→assert probes land on an exact frame rather than a generous `-n`. The stop is at the wrap back to line 0: `--screenshot` shows the picture drawn in the previous lines 1-224, while `--peek` of OAM / PPU / VRAM reads what the V-blank NMI has since written for the NEXT picture, one frame ahead. To read the state that drew the picture, stop with `--until-pc` on the NMI handler instead (see the guide)

      --until-pc <UNTIL_PC>
          Run until execution reaches this routine (then snapshot): a `.sym` label, `label+N`, or `BANK:OFFSET` in hex. The stop is just before its first instruction runs, so `--peek` reads the state the routine receives — consistent where a frame boundary falls in the middle of a game tick. `--input` scripts stay indexed by frame. Bounded by `--until-frame` when given (else 36000 frames); not reaching it is an error, exit 1. The frame and scanline of the stop are printed and land in the JSON as `until_pc`. Example: `--until-pc tickEnd --hit 120`

      --hit <HIT>
          With `--until-pc`: stop the N-th time execution reaches it (default 1, the first)
          
          [default: 1]

      --until-if <UNTIL_IF>
          With `--until-pc`: stop only at an arrival where this expression, in Mesen2's debugger language, is non-zero (`--hit N`: the N-th such arrival). Labels stand for their address, `[label]` reads a byte and `{label}` a word. The JSON's `until_pc.hits_seen` is the arrival it stopped on. Example: `--until-pc tick --until-if "[score] != 0"`

      --then-frames <THEN_FRAMES>
          With `--until-pc`: run N more frames after the stop, then take the screenshot, the `--layer-shots`, the `--peek`s and the `--out` as usual — one run per screen instead of one to find the arrival and one to capture. The scripted input and the `--poke-at`s keep going on those frames; the JSON's `until_pc` still gives the frame and the line of the arrival. Example: `--until-pc matchDecide --hit 6382 --then-frames 40 --screenshot end.png`

      --peek-at <PEEK_AT>
          Read every `--peek` EACH time execution reaches this routine (same forms as `--until-pc`), one line per arrival with its frame and scanline: a whole run's worth of consistent samples in one emulator run, with no trace code in the ROM. The run length stays `-n` / `--until-frame` / `--until-pc`. Rows go to stderr, to `--peek-at-out` as CSV, and into the JSON as `peek_hits`. Example: `--peek-at tickEnd --peek pl_x:#36 --until-frame 600`

      --peek-at-out <PEEK_AT_OUT>
          Write the `--peek-at` rows as CSV (`hit,frame,line` then one column of hex bytes per `--peek`) instead of printing them

      --poke-at <POKE_AT>
          Write every `--poke` into memory when execution reaches this routine (a `.sym` label, `label+N`, `BANK:OFFSET`), at its `--poke-hit`-th arrival, just before its first instruction: puts the game in a state it does not reach by itself, with no test code in the ROM. A `--peek-at` on the same routine reads the bytes written. Example: `--poke-at tickStart --poke-hit 91 --poke ball_x=4001 --poke ball_y=3000`. Repeatable: each `--poke-at` takes the `--poke-hit` and the `--poke`s that follow it, up to the next one

      --poke-hit <POKE_HIT>
          With `--poke-at`: the arrival the bytes are written at (default 1, the first). One per `--poke-at`

      --poke <POKE>
          Bytes to write at the `--poke-at` before it: `NAME=HEX` or `BANK:OFFSET=HEX`, the `--assert` grammar — hex bytes in memory order, so a 16-bit `$0140` is `4001`. Repeatable

      --inject-nmi-at <SPEC[:N]>
          Force an NMI just BEFORE the instruction at this routine (`SPEC` or `SPEC:N`: a `.sym` label, `label+N`, or `BANK:OFFSET`; `N` = the arrival, default 1; with a bare `BANK:OFFSET` write `BANK:OFFSET:N`). A synthetic extra edge, not hardware: the real `VBlank` NMI still comes, so a frame can see two. Not injected, with the reason, when `NMITIMEN.7` is clear. Never reached: an error. Repeatable; sweep a race by running once per `N`

      --inject-irq-at <SPEC[:N]>
          Force an IRQ just BEFORE the instruction at this routine (same `SPEC[:N]` as `--inject-nmi-at`). A single edge, `$4211` untouched. Not injected, with the reason, while the I flag is set

      --input-at <INPUT_AT>
          Index every input script (`--input` … `--input5`, `--mouse`, `--superscope`) by **arrivals on this routine** instead of by frame: entry `N:` applies the N-th time execution reaches it (a `.sym` label, `label+N`, or `BANK:OFFSET`). A frame number lands in a different game tick when the code gets faster or slower; an arrival does not, so the run depends on the game's logic alone. The press changes the controller, and the game sees it at its next read: with the auto-read, from arrival N+1. A joypad entry `N+K:` sets the mask K frames after the N-th arrival, for a screen that ignores a button held as it opens. Example: `--input-at tickStart --input "81:0x0800,96:0"`, or `--input-at screen_open --input "3+30:0x8000,3+36:0"`

      --srm-in <SRM_IN>
          Load battery SRAM from a `.srm` file before running (the other half of a power-cycle test — write it with `--srm-out` in run A, read it back in run B)

      --srm-out <SRM_OUT>
          Write battery SRAM to a `.srm` file after the run

      --apu-log <APU_LOG>
          Optional CPU↔APU mailbox traffic log. When set, every CPU read/write of `$2140-$2143` during the run is captured and written to the given path as CSV with columns: `mclk_total,frame_ntsc,pc,kind,port,value` (one row per event). Useful for diagnosing APU handshake stalls (e.g. SMW's music-driver "wait for ack" deadlock)

      --dsp-trace <DSP_TRACE>
          Optional DSP register-write trace. Captures every write to a `$00-$7F` DSP register with an SPC-cycle timestamp and writes CSV columns `spc_cycles,reg,name,value` — `name` decodes the register (`V0_ADSR1`, `KON`, `FLG`, …). Answers "did my KON/KOFF sequence reach the chip in the order I intended?", which a WAV capture cannot show

      --dsp-trace-max <DSP_TRACE_MAX>
          Cap on captured DSP register writes (see `--dsp-trace`)
          
          [default: 100000]

      --dsp-events <DSP_EVENTS>
          Optional DSP note events, JSON lines: one per voice keyed on by a `KON` (`$4C`) write, with the PPU frame number, the SPC cycle of the write and that voice's `srcn`, `pitch` (14 bits), `vol_l`, `vol_r` (signed), `adsr1`, `adsr2` and `gain`, read when the voice really starts (the end of the 5-sample KON delay, `start_spc_cycles`), so a `PITCH` written just after the `KON` is seen. A `PITCH` written later than that delay is not: use `--dsp-trace` for the full register story. A whole piece of music lines up with the picture from one command

      --dsp-events-max <DSP_EVENTS_MAX>
          Cap on captured notes (see `--dsp-events`)
          
          [default: 100000]

      --sa1-log <SA1_LOG>
          Optional SA-1 MMIO traffic log. When set, every CPU read/write of an SA-1 register `$2200-$23FF` during the run is captured and written to the given path as CSV with columns: `mclk_total,frame_ntsc,pc,kind,reg,value` (one row per event). Useful for diagnosing the CPU↔SA-1 handshake (e.g. the SMRPG intro deadlock)

      --sa1-side-log <SA1_SIDE_LOG>
          Optional SA-1-*side* execution log. When set, the SA-1's own reads/writes of its registers `$2200-$23FF` AND its *writes* to I-RAM (`$3000-$37FF`, reported as `$30xx` even via the `$0000-$07FF` mirror) are captured with the SA-1 PC and written as CSV (`seq,sa1_pc,kind,reg,value`). The I-RAM writes expose the cross-CPU handshake flags (e.g. Kirby's `$300A`/`$300E`) that the MMIO-only view can't show. Reads of I-RAM are NOT logged (they flood when the SA-1 spins on a flag). Complements `--sa1-log` (S-CPU side) to see why the SA-1 (re)asserts a register, e.g. the SMRPG SCNT=$87 loop

      --sa1-trace <SA1_TRACE>
          Optional FULL SA-1 instruction trace: a pre-opcode register snapshot per SA-1 instruction, written as CSV (`seq,pc,a,x,y,sp,p,db,dp,e`). Diff this PC stream against a bsnes/Mesen2 SA-1 trace to localise the SMRPG deadlock

      --sa1-trace-max <SA1_TRACE_MAX>
          Cap the SA-1 instruction trace at this many events (default 200 000)
          
          [default: 200000]

      --superfx-trace <SUPERFX_TRACE>
          Optional FULL Super FX (GSU) instruction trace: a per-opcode snapshot written as CSV (`seq,mclk,go,stop,pc,opcode,sfr,r0..r15`). Diff this PC/register stream against a bsnes/siena GSU trace to localise rendering divergences

      --superfx-trace-max <SUPERFX_TRACE_MAX>
          Cap the Super FX instruction trace at this many events (default 200 000)
          
          [default: 200000]

      --superfx-trace-from <SUPERFX_TRACE_FROM>
          Instruction count at which to begin the Super FX trace, like `--dma-trace-from` (an instruction count, not a frame: for frame N, take `stats.instructions_executed` from `luna state --until-frame N --out -`). The trace is a ring that keeps the most recent events once full, so the run's end picks the window; this trims its head, giving exactly [from, end] as long as that fits under `--superfx-trace-max`
          
          [default: 0]

      --gsu-bus-trace <GSU_BUS_TRACE>
          Optional Super FX bus-ownership trace: every CPU read of Game Pak ROM or RAM made while the GSU owned it, as CSV (`seq,frame,line,mclk,pc,addr,kind`). Those reads return the busy vector or open bus — silently, on hardware too — so this names the instruction that did it. `gsu.bus_violations` in `--out -` counts them without the trace

      --gsu-bus-trace-max <GSU_BUS_TRACE_MAX>
          Cap the Super FX bus-ownership trace (default 200 000)
          
          [default: 200000]

      --dsp1-trace <DSP1_TRACE>
          Optional DSP-1 (`µPD77C25`) trace: microcode execution AND the CPU-side DR/SR port traffic in ONE interleaved stream, as CSV (`seq,kind,pc,opcode,value,a,b,dr,sr,rqm`). `kind` is E/W/R/S (exec, DR write, DR read, SR poll) — so the command handshake is readable directly: did the byte land before or after RQM cleared? Parity with `--superfx-trace` / `--sa1-trace`

      --dsp1-trace-max <DSP1_TRACE_MAX>
          Cap the DSP-1 trace at this many events (default 200 000)
          
          [default: 200000]

      --dsp1-trace-ports
          Restrict `--dsp1-trace` to the CPU-side DR/SR transactions, dropping microcode execution. The stock firmware idles in an RQM wait loop, so a full trace is almost entirely idle spin and the cap is exhausted before the interesting command lands — use this to read the command handshake itself

      --dsp1-trace-commands <DSP1_TRACE_COMMANDS>
          Group the DSP-1 port trace into command transactions, as CSV (`seq,cmd,name,pc,in_words,out_words,expected_in,expected_out, confidence,status,in,out`). One row per command: the byte, the input words it consumed, the output words it produced.
          
          Transaction boundaries come from the protocol (an 8-bit `DRC` write opens a command), never from the word-count table — so a stale table entry surfaces as `status=mismatch` on that one row instead of silently mis-grouping the rest. `confidence` says how far the expected counts can be trusted; open-ended operations (Raster, ROM dump) report their observed length and assert nothing. Implies `--dsp1-trace-ports`.

      --spc-trace <SPC_TRACE>
          Optional FULL SPC700 instruction trace: a per-opcode register snapshot written as CSV (`seq,pc,a,x,y,sp,psw,spc_cycle,t2_int,t2_out`). Diff this PC stream against a Mesen2 SPC700 trace to localise audio-driver (Akao CPU↔SPC handshake) divergences (e.g. SMRPG/CT)

      --spc-trace-max <SPC_TRACE_MAX>
          Cap the SPC700 instruction trace at this many events (default 200 000)
          
          [default: 200000]

      --cpu-trace <CPU_TRACE>
          Optional CPU instruction trace. When set, captures a per-instruction register snapshot (PC, A, X, Y, SP, P, DB, DP, e) into the given CSV file. Capture starts at instr count `--cpu-trace-from` (default 0) and stops after `--cpu-trace-max` events (default 100 000). Memory cost is ≈ 40 bytes × max-events

      --cpu-trace-from <CPU_TRACE_FROM>
          Instruction count at which to begin populating `--cpu-trace`. Default 0 (= capture from the very first step). Set to a value near the scene you want to debug to keep the buffer small
          
          [default: 0]

      --cpu-trace-max <CPU_TRACE_MAX>
          Max number of trace events to capture (hard cap on log size). Default 100 000 ≈ 4 MB CSV
          
          [default: 100000]

      --mem-trace <MEM_TRACE>
          Optional memory access trace. When set, captures every CPU bus read/write into a CSV at PATH, columns `mclk_total,frame_ntsc,pc,addr,kind,value,line,hclock,blank,force_blank,origin,symbol` (`line` / `hclock` = the beam position, `blank` = V-blank, `force_blank` = INIDISP `$2100` bit 7 at the access; a VRAM write is safe iff `blank||force_blank`; `origin` = `cpu`, `dma<n>` or `hdma<n>`; `symbol` = the nearest label at or below the PC, empty without a `.sym`). Default: all banks. Combine with `--mem-trace-bank 7E` to focus on WRAM and skip ROM fetches. Gated by `--mem-trace-from` and `--mem-trace-max` analogous to `--cpu-trace-*`

      --mem-trace-from <MEM_TRACE_FROM>
          [default: 0]

      --mem-trace-max <MEM_TRACE_MAX>
          [default: 100000]

      --mem-trace-bank <MEM_TRACE_BANK>
          Hex bank to filter the memory trace on (e.g. `7E` for WRAM main page). Omit to capture every access

      --mem-trace-addr <MEM_TRACE_ADDR>
          Hex offset range `LO:HI` (inclusive) to filter the memory trace on, e.g. `2100:21FF` to capture only PPU/CPU MMIO across all banks without the bank filter's code-fetch flood. Composes with `--mem-trace-bank` (both must match)

      --trace-writes <TRACE_WRITES>
          The "who wrote this register" hunt: record only WRITES to these hex offsets (any bank), e.g. `2121,2122,420C`. Each row's `origin` column says who — `cpu`, `dma<n>` or `hdma<n>` — with the frame / line / PC. The interrupt markers stay in the CSV to place the writes in time: `kind` `N` (NMI, at `$4210`) and `I` (IRQ, at `$4211`) — filter on `kind` `W` to count writes. Composes with `--mem-trace-bank`; needs `--mem-trace <PATH>`

      --dma-trace <DMA_TRACE>
          Optional DMA→VRAM transfer-time trace. Captures every byte an MDMA writes to `$2118/$2119` as CSV (`seq,frame,line,blank,force_blank,src,vram_word,reg,value`) — `blank` = V-blank period, `force_blank` = INIDISP (`$2100`) bit 7 at the write (a write is safe iff `blank||force_blank`), `src` the 24-bit A-bus source, `vram_word` the VMADD word the byte lands at, `reg` $18/$19. The byte is captured AS READ during the transfer, so a coprocessor (Super FX) overwriting its source buffer afterwards can't confound the source→VRAM comparison. Gated by `--dma-trace-from`/`--dma-trace-max`

      --dma-trace-from <DMA_TRACE_FROM>
          Instruction count at which to begin the DMA→VRAM trace
          
          [default: 0]

      --dma-trace-max <DMA_TRACE_MAX>
          Max DMA→VRAM trace events (default 500 000)
          
          [default: 500000]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```


## `luna frames`

```text
Capture a sequence of EXACTLY-consecutive PPU frames as PNGs in one run, via the same `luna-api` render path the GUI uses. Use this to diagnose *temporal* artefacts (flicker / double-buffer page-flip desync) that a single `state --screenshot` cannot show — it samples one frame, so a frame-to-frame "blink" is invisible to it. Each frame's PNG is tagged with its frame number and the INIDISP forced-blank flag, so you can see exactly what the GUI would (and would not) display

Usage: luna frames [OPTIONS] <ROM>

Arguments:
  <ROM>  Path to the .sfc / .smc ROM file

Options:
  -n, --steps <STEPS>                Warm-up CPU instructions to execute before capturing begins [default: 1000]
      --from-frame <FROM_FRAME>      Start the capture at PPU frame N instead of after the `-n` warm-up instructions (which are then ignored) — the first PNG is frame N. Frame-indexed like `state --until-frame`, so the sequence is stable across codegen changes
  -c, --count <COUNT>                Number of consecutive frames to capture [default: 8]
      --out-dir <OUT_DIR>            Output directory for the PNG sequence (created if absent) [default: /tmp/luna_frames]
      --force-mapper <FORCE_MAPPER>  Force a cartridge mapper, bypassing header auto-detection. One of: lorom, hirom, exhirom, sa1, superfx, dsp1, sdd1; spc7110 is recognised but not emulated, the load refuses it
      --force-region <FORCE_REGION>  Force the video standard (ntsc, pal), overriding the cartridge header's country byte. Changes the scanline count (262/312) and frame rate — required to reproduce the golden harness, which runs the `PeterLemon` corpus as PAL to match krom's reference captures
      --power-on <POWER_ON>          What RAM holds before the ROM boots: `zero` (default), `ones`, `random` (a seed is derived and printed) or `random=<seed>` (decimal or 0x hex — replays an exact machine). Fills WRAM, VRAM, CGRAM, OAM, APU RAM and the cartridge RAM no battery keeps (Game Pak RAM, BW-RAM, I-RAM); a boot bug that only shows on real hardware's garbage RAM shows here too
      --input <INPUT>                Scripted joypad-1 input, same `frame:hex` format as `state --input`, applied during the warm-up so the capture can land in gameplay rather than at a title screen
  -h, --help                         Print help
```


## `luna record`

```text
Record a run as a small video, a text timeline and contact sheets: `<OUT>.mp4` (H.264 + AAC, the picture at twice its size with a strip under it naming the frame, the time and the buttons held), `<OUT>.md` (when the picture moves, holds or goes off, when the pad changes, the sound second by second) and `<OUT>-1.png` … (one labelled picture per second). The video is for eyes and for the models that take one; the text and the sheets are for the ones that do not. The video needs `ffmpeg` on the machine; `--no-video` writes the rest without it. Exit 0 = written, 1 = the run or the encoder failed, 2 = usage error

Usage: luna record [OPTIONS] <ROM>

Arguments:
  <ROM>  Path to the .sfc / .smc ROM file

Options:
  -o, --out <OUT>                    Base path of the files written: `--out /tmp/demo` gives `/tmp/demo.mp4`, `/tmp/demo.md`, `/tmp/demo-1.png` … (a trailing `.mp4` is dropped)
      --raw <FILE|->                 Write the bare picture instead of the video: every frame as raw RGB (3 bytes a dot), 512 dots wide, rows as the screen draws them, to this file or to stdout (`-`). No strip, no timeline, no sheets, no `ffmpeg`. The size and the rate are said on stderr as one JSON line before the first frame, the sound rate in a second one at the end
      --raw-audio <RAW_AUDIO>        With `--raw`: where the sound goes, 16-bit stereo little-endian PCM (default: `<OUT>.pcm` when `--out` is given, else none)
      --from-frame <FROM_FRAME>      First PPU frame recorded, frame-indexed like `state --until-frame` [default: 1]
  -c, --count <COUNT>                Number of consecutive frames recorded (600 is ten seconds of NTSC) [default: 600]
      --sheet-every <SHEET_EVERY>    Frames between two pictures of the contact sheets. Default: one per second (60 on NTSC, 50 on PAL)
      --video-kbps <VIDEO_KBPS>      Bitrate the picture is held to, in kbit/s: what bounds the size of the file (at 500, a minute weighs 3 to 5 MB with its sound; a busy scene is soft at that rate and sharp at 1000) [default: 500]
      --ffmpeg <FFMPEG>              The `ffmpeg` to run [default: ffmpeg]
      --no-video                     Write the timeline and the contact sheets only: no video, and no `ffmpeg` needed
      --force-mapper <FORCE_MAPPER>  Force a cartridge mapper, bypassing header auto-detection. One of: lorom, hirom, exhirom, sa1, superfx, dsp1, sdd1; spc7110 is recognised but not emulated, the load refuses it
      --force-region <FORCE_REGION>  Force the video standard (ntsc, pal), overriding the cartridge header's country byte
      --power-on <POWER_ON>          What RAM holds before the ROM boots: `zero` (default), `ones`, `random` (a seed is derived and printed) or `random=<seed>`
      --input <INPUT>                Scripted joypad-1 input, same `frame:hex` format as `state --input`; an event before `--from-frame` is applied on its frame during the warm-up
      --input2 <INPUT2>              Scripted joypad-2 input (`state --input2` grammar)
      --input-at <INPUT_AT>          Index the input scripts by arrivals on this routine instead of by frame (`state --input-at`; `N+K:` = K frames after arrival N)
      --poke-at <POKE_AT>            Write every `--poke` into memory when execution reaches this routine, at its `--poke-hit`-th arrival counted from power-on (`state --poke-at`): record a scene the game only reaches through a menu. Repeatable: each `--poke-at` takes the `--poke-hit` and the `--poke`s that follow it
      --poke-hit <POKE_HIT>          With `--poke-at`: the arrival the bytes are written at (default 1, the first). One per `--poke-at`
      --poke <POKE>                  Bytes to write at the `--poke-at` before it: `NAME=HEX` or `BANK:OFFSET=HEX`, hex bytes in memory order. Repeatable
      --inject-nmi-at <SPEC[:N]>     Force an NMI just BEFORE the instruction at this routine (`SPEC` or `SPEC:N`: a `.sym` label, `label+N`, or `BANK:OFFSET`; `N` = the arrival, default 1; with a bare `BANK:OFFSET` write `BANK:OFFSET:N`). A synthetic extra edge, not hardware: the real `VBlank` NMI still comes, so a frame can see two. Not injected, with the reason, when `NMITIMEN.7` is clear. Never reached: an error. Repeatable; sweep a race by running once per `N`
      --inject-irq-at <SPEC[:N]>     Force an IRQ just BEFORE the instruction at this routine (same `SPEC[:N]` as `--inject-nmi-at`). A single edge, `$4211` untouched. Not injected, with the reason, while the I flag is set
      --sym <SYM>                    Symbol file naming the routines and variables of `--poke-at`, `--poke` and `--input-at`. Default: the `.sym` beside the ROM
  -h, --help                         Print help
```


## `luna diff`

```text
Compare two ROMs frame by frame: run both in one process, hash the displayed frame at every PPU frame, and print MATCH / DIFF for each requested frame — MATCH when A's frame `F` equals B's frame at some `F ± tolerance` (the boot-length offset a codegen change can introduce). The "compare at equal frame" protocol that validates a compiler / library change. Exit 0 = all match, 1 = any DIFF, 2 = usage error.

With `--audio`, the two ROMs' sound is compared instead: both run to `--until-frame`, the output is cut into windows and each window's RMS level compared. MATCH when every window is within `--tolerance-pct` — the comparison that survives the same sound arriving a few samples earlier or later, which an audio hash does not.

With `--sequence`, time is ignored: every frame of `--from`..`--to` is hashed, each run of identical frames counts as one picture, and the longest run of pictures both ROMs show in the same order is measured. SAME-SEQUENCE when it reaches `--min-common` — the same animation at another cadence, or after a boot of another length.

Usage: luna diff [OPTIONS] <ROM_A> <ROM_B>

Arguments:
  <ROM_A>
          The reference build

  <ROM_B>
          The build under test

Options:
      --frames <FRAMES>
          PPU frames to compare, comma-separated (e.g. `200,400`)

      --tolerance <TOLERANCE>
          Accept a match up to this many frames away (`b = a ± n`)
          
          [default: 0]

      --sequence
          Compare the sequence of pictures over a range of frames instead of the frames one by one

      --from <FROM>
          `--sequence`: first PPU frame of the range [default: 1]

      --to <TO>
          `--sequence`: last PPU frame of the range

      --min-common <MIN_COMMON>
          `--sequence`: SAME-SEQUENCE when the longest common run holds at least this many pictures

      --min-common-pct <MIN_COMMON_PCT>
          `--sequence`: SAME-SEQUENCE when the longest common run holds at least this percentage of the pictures of the ROM that shows fewer of them [default: 90]

      --audio
          Compare the audio output instead of the displayed frames

      --until-frame <UNTIL_FRAME>
          `--audio`: run both ROMs to this PPU frame

      --window-ms <WINDOW_MS>
          `--audio`: window length, in milliseconds of output [default: 500]

      --tolerance-pct <TOLERANCE_PCT>
          `--audio`: largest RMS difference a window may show, in percent of the louder of the two [default: 2]

      --align-onset
          `--audio`: compare each window with the stretch of the other ROM's output that fits it best within `--max-shift` samples, and print the shift kept — for the same sounds, each a few samples earlier or later

      --max-shift <MAX_SHIFT>
          `--align-onset`: how far a window may be moved, in samples. A frame is 534 [default: 64]

      --silence <SILENCE>
          `--audio`: sample level counted as silence (0-32767). It is the threshold of the reported onset, and the floor a window's difference is measured against [default: 64]

      --input <INPUT>
          Scripted joypad-1 input applied to BOTH machines (`state --input` grammar)

      --screenshot-dir <SCREENSHOT_DIR>
          Write `frame_<F>_a.png` / `frame_<F>_b.png` here for every DIFF frame

      --out <OUT>
          Also write a JSON report (`-` = stdout after the text lines)

      --force-display
          Hash the frame with INIDISP forced-blank bypassed (as `run --force-display`)

      --native-res
          Hash the native 512×448 frame

      --force-mapper <FORCE_MAPPER>
          Force a cartridge mapper for both ROMs. One of: lorom, hirom, exhirom, sa1, superfx, dsp1, sdd1; spc7110 is recognised but not emulated, the load refuses it

      --force-region <FORCE_REGION>
          Force the video standard for both ROMs (ntsc, pal)

      --power-on <POWER_ON>
          Power-on RAM state for both machines (`zero`, `ones`, `random[=<seed>]`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```


## `luna profile`

```text
Real master cycles per symbol: every step credits its cycles — bus + internal cycles plus the DMA / HDMA / refresh stalls charged during it — to the instruction's address; the report folds those onto the nearest `.sym` label (or a 256-byte page without one), heaviest first. Replaces static instruction weights with what the machine paid

Usage: luna profile [OPTIONS] <ROM>

Arguments:
  <ROM>  Path to the .sfc / .smc ROM file

Options:
  -n, --steps <STEPS>
          CPU instructions to profile (after `--from-frame`) [default: 3000000]
      --until-frame <UNTIL_FRAME>
          Profile until PPU frame N instead of the `-n` count
      --from-frame <FROM_FRAME>
          Start profiling at PPU frame N (warm-up before it is not counted) — e.g. skip the boot to profile the game loop [default: 0]
      --input <INPUT>
          Scripted joypad-1 input (`state --input` grammar)
      --input2 <INPUT2>
          Scripted joypad-2 input (`state --input2` grammar)
      --input3 <INPUT3>
          Multitap pads B, C, D — players 3, 4, 5 (`state --input3`)
      --input4 <INPUT4>
          Player 4 (multitap pad C) — see `--input3`
      --input5 <INPUT5>
          Player 5 (multitap pad D) — see `--input3`
      --port1 <PORT1>
          Controller port-1 device: `pad` (default), `mouse`, `superscope`, `multitap`, or `none` for an unplugged port (its data lines read 0 for ever, where a pad's idle high — auto-read cannot tell them apart, only a manual read past bit 15 can) [default: pad]
      --port2 <PORT2>
          Controller port-2 device: `pad` (default), `mouse`, `superscope`, `multitap`, or `none` for an unplugged port — see `--port1` [default: pad]
      --mouse <MOUSE>
          Scripted SNES Mouse motion (`state --mouse` grammar), applied to whichever port is set to `mouse`
      --superscope <SUPERSCOPE>
          Scripted Super Scope aim (`state --superscope` grammar), applied to whichever port is set to `superscope`
      --sym <SYM>
          WLA-DX `.sym` to fold PCs onto (overrides the `<rom>.sym` auto-detection)
      --top <TOP>
          Rows to print (the JSON report always has them all) [default: 25]
      --out <OUT>
          Write the full report as JSON (`-` = stdout after the table)
      --pc-set <PC_SET>
          Write the set of executed 24-bit PCs (sorted, deduplicated, little-endian `u32` each) to this file — the input a code-coverage tool folds onto symbols and source lines. Whole 24-bit space: `HiROM` `$C0-$FF`, `FastROM` mirrors and WRAM-resident code included
      --budget <BUDGET>
          Gate: `SYMBOL=MCLK` — the symbol's worst completed frame must not exceed MCLK master cycles, else exit 1 (repeatable; an unknown symbol is a usage error, exit 2). The VBlank-budget check for CI: `--budget NmiHandler=6000`
      --stack-floor <STACK_FLOOR>
          Gate: the stack must never reach below this address, else exit 1 — the RAM-budget check a link-time guess cannot make (`--stack-floor 0x1C60`). Accepts `0x`- or `$`-hex, or decimal. The figure is reported either way, with the routine that went deepest when a `.sym` is loaded
      --gsu-pc-set <GSU_PC_SET>
          Write the set of executed **GSU** PCs (same encoding as `--pc-set`): a separate file, because a GSU PC and a 65816 PC can be the same number and mean different code — merging them would mis-attribute coverage. Lets a coverage tool count `.sfx`
      --input-at <INPUT_AT>
          Index the input scripts by arrivals on this routine instead of by frame (`state --input-at`): the same script then drives two builds of a game through the same ticks, whatever their speed (`N+K:` = K frames after arrival N)
      --poke-at <POKE_AT>
          Write every `--poke` into memory when execution reaches this routine, at its `--poke-hit`-th arrival counted from power-on, just before its first instruction (`state --poke-at`): profile a scene the game only reaches through a menu. Repeatable: each `--poke-at` takes the `--poke-hit` and the `--poke`s that follow it. Example: `--poke-at main --poke skip_menu=01`
      --poke-hit <POKE_HIT>
          With `--poke-at`: the arrival the bytes are written at (default 1, the first). One per `--poke-at`
      --poke <POKE>
          Bytes to write at the `--poke-at` before it: `NAME=HEX` or `BANK:OFFSET=HEX`, hex bytes in memory order. Repeatable
      --inject-nmi-at <SPEC[:N]>
          Force an NMI just BEFORE the instruction at this routine (`SPEC` or `SPEC:N`: a `.sym` label, `label+N`, or `BANK:OFFSET`; `N` = the arrival, default 1; with a bare `BANK:OFFSET` write `BANK:OFFSET:N`). A synthetic extra edge, not hardware: the real `VBlank` NMI still comes, so a frame can see two. Not injected, with the reason, when `NMITIMEN.7` is clear. Never reached: an error. Repeatable; sweep a race by running once per `N`
      --inject-irq-at <SPEC[:N]>
          Force an IRQ just BEFORE the instruction at this routine (same `SPEC[:N]` as `--inject-nmi-at`). A single edge, `$4211` untouched. Not injected, with the reason, while the I flag is set
      --until-pc <UNTIL_PC>
          End the profile when execution reaches this routine (a `.sym` label, `label+N`, or `BANK:OFFSET` in hex), just before its first instruction: a window of N game ticks rather than N frames, which stays the same work when the code gets faster. Bounded by `--until-frame` when given (else 36000 frames; `-n` does not apply); not reaching it is an error, exit 1. Example: `--from-frame 60 --until-pc tickEnd --hit 340`
      --hit <HIT>
          With `--until-pc`: which arrival, counted from power-on [default: 1]
      --frames-out <FRAMES_OUT>
          Write the window frame by frame as CSV (`frame,active_mclk,idle_mclk,cpu_mclk,dma_mclk,hdma_mclk,refresh_mclk,total_mclk,nmi,lag,refresh_in_wai_mclk`): `active` is what the program used (CPU + the DMA it started), `idle` the time parked in `WAI`, `refresh_in_wai` the DRAM refresh that fell while parked (idle + it = the time parked), `lag` = full frame: the NMI found the CPU still executing (it is NOT the duration of a game tick: a two-frame tick lags every other frame by design; see `luna ticks --intervals`). The same rows are `frame_series` in `--out`. Finds WHICH frame overran, in one run
      --worst <WORST>
          Print the per-symbol table of the N heaviest frames (by `active_mclk`), and put them in `--out` as `worst_frames` — what was running in the frame that overran [default: 0]
      --max-frame-mclk <MAX_FRAME_MCLK>
          Gate: no completed frame may use more than N active master cycles, else exit 1
      --max-lag-frames <MAX_LAG_FRAMES>
          Gate: at most N lag frames in the window, else exit 1. A lag frame is a FULL frame: its NMI came while the CPU was executing rather than parked in `WAI`. It does not measure how long a game tick lasts (`luna ticks --intervals` does)
      --max-lag-run <MAX_LAG_RUN>
          Gate: at most N lag frames (full frames, not tick durations) IN A ROW, else exit 1. A game whose tick takes two frames lags every other frame by design: `--max-lag-run 1` passes it and fails the tick that spills into a third
      --no-render
          Leave the picture uncomputed: the same cycles and the same report, in about half the time. A profile never reads the screen
      --force-mapper <FORCE_MAPPER>
          Force a cartridge mapper. One of: lorom, hirom, exhirom, sa1, superfx, dsp1, sdd1; spc7110 is recognised but not emulated, the load refuses it
      --force-region <FORCE_REGION>
          Force the video standard (ntsc, pal)
      --power-on <POWER_ON>
          Power-on RAM state (`zero`, `ones`, `random[=<seed>]`)
  -h, --help
          Print help
```


## `luna ticks`

```text
Record named memory zones at every tick of a game, as JSONL in the `tick-record` format (version 1): a header line, one line per tick, and an end line a complete record always has. A tick is an arrival on a routine the spec names, read just before its first instruction, so two runs line up tick by tick whatever their speed — two builds of a game, or a port and the program it reproduces, recorded by another emulator in the same format. The zones are raw bytes in memory order; the header gives the byte order. Exit 0 = the record is complete, 1 = the run fell short of it (the end line says why), 2 = the spec was refused and nothing ran.

`--compare A B` compares two records instead (no ROM, no spec) and reports the first tick where a zone differs: exit 0 = identical, 1 = they diverge, 2 = they cannot be compared.

Usage: luna ticks [OPTIONS] [ROM]

Arguments:
  [ROM]
          Path to the .sfc / .smc ROM file

Options:
      --spec <SPEC>
          The spec (TOML): the tick routine, the zones, and optionally a start point, a limit, an input script, pokes and pictures. See the guide for every key

      --compare <A> <B>
          Compare two records (JSONL files, `-` for one of them on stdin) and report the first tick where a zone differs. Pairs ticks by `t`; the clock fields are never compared. Exit 0 = identical, 1 = they diverge, 2 = they cannot be compared

      --intervals <RECORD>
          The duration of each tick of a record already written (by luna or by any program that writes the format; `-` for stdin): from one arrival on the tick routine to the next, in frames and milliseconds, with the longest tick. This is NOT `luna profile`'s lag (a frame whose NMI found the CPU executing, which a two-frame tick has every other frame by design). A luna record converts by its header; any other `clock.cycles` unit needs `--frame-cycles`. Exit 0 = measured, 2 = cannot be measured

      --frame-cycles <FRAME_CYCLES>
          With `--intervals`: cycles of one frame in the record's `clock.cycles` unit. Required unless the record is luna's (`snes_master` at the NTSC or PAL rate, from which it is known)

      --cycle-hz <CYCLE_HZ>
          With `--intervals`: cycles per second of that unit, for the milliseconds (default: the header's rate for a luna record; otherwise no milliseconds)

      --over <OVER>
          With `--intervals`: list the ticks lasting more than N frames (fractional: `2.5` lists the ticks that spilled into a third)

      --csv <CSV>
          With `--compare`: write every differing zone of every tick as CSV (`t,zone,first_offset,a,b,differing_bytes`) to this file, `-` for stdout. With `--intervals`: one row per tick, `t,frame_delta,cycles,frames,ms,over`

      --zone <ZONE>
          With `--compare`: compare only this zone (repeatable). Without it, both records must name the same zones

      --out <OUT>
          Where the record goes; `-` is stdout
          
          [default: -]

      --shots-dir <SHOTS_DIR>
          Folder of the `[shots]` pictures (default: `<OUT>.shots`)

      --audio-out <AUDIO_OUT>
          A 16-bit stereo WAV of the sound of the `every_frame` pictures: the same frames, counted from the same anchor tick, not from power-on. Needs `[shots] every_frame = true`

      --schema
          Print the JSON Schema of the three kinds of line and exit — no ROM needed

      --sym <SYM>
          WLA-DX `.sym` file (default: `<ROM>.sym` when it exists)

      --force-mapper <FORCE_MAPPER>
          Force a cartridge mapper. One of: lorom, hirom, exhirom, sa1, superfx, dsp1, sdd1; spc7110 is recognised but not emulated, the load refuses it

      --force-region <FORCE_REGION>
          Force the video standard (ntsc, pal)

      --power-on <POWER_ON>
          Power-on RAM state (`zero`, `ones`, `random[=<seed>]`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```


## `luna wram-trace`

```text
Emit per-frame (vblank-aligned) WRAM page hashes for a confound-free cross-emulator differential. Each line is `<ppu_frame> <h0> <h1> ... <hN>` where each `h` is the FNV-1a hash of one WRAM page (`--page-size` bytes, default 4 KiB → 32 pages). Because WRAM-at-vblank-N is the SAME game-frame in both luna and a reference emulator (no input ⟹ game logic advances once per NMI), the first frame whose page hash differs from the reference pins the first REAL state divergence — unlike scene- level windows the boot-frame offset confounds

Usage: luna wram-trace [OPTIONS] <ROM>

Arguments:
  <ROM>  Path to the .sfc / .smc ROM file

Options:
  -n, --steps <STEPS>                Warm-up CPU instructions before frame-0 of the trace [default: 0]
  -c, --count <COUNT>                Number of consecutive frames to hash [default: 300]
      --page-size <PAGE_SIZE>        WRAM page size in bytes (power of two dividing 0x20000) [default: 4096]
      --out <OUT>                    Output path for the hash table (one line per frame) [default: /tmp/luna_wram_hashes.txt]
      --dump-frame <DUMP_FRAME>      Optionally also dump the full 128 KiB WRAM as a raw .bin when the trace reaches this PPU frame (for byte-level diffing)
      --dump-out <DUMP_OUT>          Output path for the `--dump-frame` raw WRAM snapshot [default: /tmp/luna_wram_frame.bin]
      --force-mapper <FORCE_MAPPER>  Force a cartridge mapper. One of: lorom, hirom, exhirom, sa1, superfx, dsp1, sdd1; spc7110 is recognised but not emulated, the load refuses it
      --force-region <FORCE_REGION>  Force the video standard (ntsc, pal), overriding the cartridge header's country byte. Changes the scanline count (262/312) and frame rate — required to reproduce the golden harness, which runs the `PeterLemon` corpus as PAL to match krom's reference captures
      --input <INPUT>                Scripted joypad-1 input, same `frame:hex` format as `state --input`
  -h, --help                         Print help
```


## `luna bench`

```text
Run every ROM in a directory headless, detect anomalies (crashes, freezes, dead APU, missing firmware), and write a compatibility report + one markdown bug file per finding. Stresses the CLI/API across the whole corpus. Reports stay local (under `--out`)

Usage: luna bench [OPTIONS] [DIR]

Arguments:
  [DIR]  Directory of ROMs to scan (`.sfc` / `.smc`) [default: tests/roms]

Options:
      --out <OUT>        Output directory for the report, screenshots, and bug files [default: tests/roms/bench]
  -f, --frames <FRAMES>  Frames to run per ROM [default: 600]
      --input <INPUT>    Override the default Start-pulse input (`frame:hex`, like `state --input`) applied to clear title screens
      --jobs <JOBS>      Bench up to N ROMs at once (0 = one per CPU). Each ROM gets its own emulator; the progress lines, the report and the bug files are the same, in the same order, as a serial run [default: 1]
  -h, --help             Print help
```


## `luna race-sweep`

```text
Search the interrupt races of a routine: force an NMI (or an IRQ) before EACH instruction of `--from`..`--to`, from one snapshot, and compare the outcome with the run that was not interrupted. Warm up (`--warm-until-pc` / `--warm-frames`), snapshot, run the baseline to the end condition (`--until-pc` / `--until-frame`), read the `--compare` bytes, then for every instruction address of the range the baseline executed: restore, interrupt there, run to the same end, compare. A trial is identical, DIFFERS (the bytes are listed), NOT TAKEN (injection refused: NMITIMEN.7 clear, I flag set; never a pass) or END NOT REACHED (a hang, a lost wake-up). The injected edge is synthetic, as for `--inject-nmi-at`. Deterministic: the report is the same for any `--jobs`. The window must hold no interrupt of its own (a natural NMI): the baseline counts them and the sweep is refused unless `--allow-baseline-interrupt` (then NESTED trials).

Exit 0 = report printed, 1 = with `--fail-on-race`: a race was found (or every injection was refused), 2 = usage error.

Usage: luna race-sweep [OPTIONS] --from <SPEC> --to <SPEC> <ROM>

Arguments:
  <ROM>
          Path to the .sfc / .smc ROM file

Options:
      --sym <SYM>
          Symbol file naming the routines and variables. Default: the `.sym` beside the ROM

      --from <SPEC>
          First instruction address swept (a `.sym` label, `label+N`, or `BANK:OFFSET` in hex)

      --to <SPEC>
          Last address swept, inclusive (same forms)

      --kind <KIND>
          Interrupt forced at each address: nmi, irq or both
          
          [default: nmi]

      --hit <HIT>
          Inject at this arrival of each address (default 1); an address the baseline reaches fewer times is not swept
          
          [default: 1]

      --warm-until-pc <SPEC>
          Start the sweep at the arrival on this routine (the machine is snapshotted there). Default: right after reset

      --warm-hit <WARM_HIT>
          With --warm-until-pc: the arrival (default 1)
          
          [default: 1]

      --warm-frames <N>
          Start the sweep at this absolute frame number

      --until-pc <SPEC>
          End of every run: the arrival on this routine

      --until-hit <UNTIL_HIT>
          With --until-pc: the arrival (default 1, counted from the snapshot; standing on it counts)
          
          [default: 1]

      --until-frame <N>
          End of every run: this absolute frame number

      --compare <SPEC[:COUNT]>
          Bytes that must be equal at the end: `SPEC` or `SPEC:COUNT` (`BANK:OFFSET` in hex, or a symbol; a symbol's count defaults to its size in the `.sym`; with a bare `BANK:OFFSET` write `BANK:OFFSET:COUNT`). Repeatable

      --max-steps <MAX_STEPS>
          Instruction budget of the baseline, and the cap of a trial (a trial gets 4x the baseline + 100000, within this)
          
          [default: 20000000]

      --allow-baseline-interrupt
          Run although the window takes a real interrupt by itself (a natural NMI): without it the sweep is refused (exit 2), since every trial would add a second interrupt the hardware cannot give. With it, the addresses the baseline runs inside the handler are NESTED (not run, never a race) and the report warns that the other trials stack a second interrupt

      --jobs <JOBS>
          Trials in parallel (0 = one per CPU). Same report for any value
          
          [default: 1]

      --json
          Print the report as JSON (schema 1) instead of text

      --out <OUT>
          Write the report to this file instead of stdout

      --fail-on-race
          Exit 1 when a race was found (a trial differs or loses its end) or when every injection was refused

      --force-mapper <FORCE_MAPPER>
          Force a cartridge mapper, bypassing header auto-detection. One of: lorom, hirom, exhirom, sa1, superfx, dsp1, sdd1; spc7110 is recognised but not emulated, the load refuses it

      --force-region <FORCE_REGION>
          Force the video standard (ntsc, pal)

      --power-on <POWER_ON>
          What RAM holds before the ROM boots (zero, ones, random, random=<seed>)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```


## `luna audio-check`

```text
Audio fault analyzer: find a gap (a hole in a sound that was playing), a click (a jump out of the slope of the signal), saturation (clipped runs) and, with --voices-dir, a voice cut (a voice that falls to silence with no release decay) in a WAV written by `luna state --audio-out` (and `--voice-wav-dir`). One line per fault (kind, frame, time, measured numbers, threshold name), or --json (schema 1). Frames are nominal: a WAV has no frame marks. It reads the core's stream, not the host's resampling or pacing.

Exit 0 = clean, 1 = at least one fault of a --fail-on kind, 2 = usage or I/O error.

Usage: luna audio-check [OPTIONS] <WAV>

Arguments:
  <WAV>
          The WAV to analyse (16-bit PCM, mono or stereo)

Options:
      --voices-dir <VOICES_DIR>
          Directory holding voice0.wav .. voice7.wav (`state --voice-wav-dir`): enables the voice-cut check

      --region <REGION>
          Video region, which sets the nominal frame length: ntsc (default, ~533.1 samples at 32040 Hz) or pal (~640.7)
          
          [default: ntsc]

      --json
          Print the report as JSON (schema 1)

      --fail-on <FAIL_ON>
          Comma-separated kinds that fail the exit code (gap, click, saturation, voice-cut). Default: gap,click,saturation (a voice cut is listed, but the hardware does the same at the end of an unlooped BRR sample, so it fails only when asked for)

      --gap-floor <GAP_FLOOR>
          A stretch is silent below this RMS (default 16)

      --gap-level <GAP_LEVEL>
          The sound before a gap must average at least this RMS (default 256)

      --gap-before <GAP_BEFORE>
          Frames of sound required before a gap (default 3)

      --gap-min-frames <GAP_MIN_FRAMES>
          Shortest gap, in frames (default 0.75)

      --gap-max-frames <GAP_MAX_FRAMES>
          Longest gap, in frames; longer is a pause (default 60)

      --gap-edge-ratio <GAP_EDGE_RATIO>
          Gap start: the RMS of the 32 samples before the hole must be this fraction of the sound's level; a musical rest fades out and fails it (default 0.35)

      --click-ratio <CLICK_RATIO>
          Click: second difference over the local mean (default 40)

      --click-floor <CLICK_FLOOR>
          Click: smallest second difference, absolute (default 4000)

      --sat-run <SAT_RUN>
          Saturation: consecutive samples at the rails (default 4)

      --voice-level <VOICE_LEVEL>
          Voice cut: the voice peaked above this (default 2000)

      --voice-cut-samples <VOICE_CUT_SAMPLES>
          Voice cut: falls to silence in fewer samples than this (default 32)

      --voice-decay-ratio <VOICE_DECAY_RATIO>
          Voice cut: a release decay leaves less than this fraction of the earlier peak in the last samples (default 0.25)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```


## `luna cart-check`

```text
Audit a ROM's header for a physical cartridge (repro board / flash): copier header, checksum, sizes, map byte, vectors, SRAM and chipset, country, title. One line per finding, `SEVERITY CODE: message`.

Exit 0 = no Error/Warn (Info allowed), 1 = at least one Error/Warn, 2 = the file cannot be read.

Usage: luna cart-check [OPTIONS] <ROM>

Arguments:
  <ROM>
          Path to the .sfc / .smc ROM file

Options:
      --json
          Print the findings as JSON instead of text

      --no-sram
          Refuse any declared save RAM (SRAM size byte or a RAM/battery chipset): `ERROR SRAM_DECLARED`. For cartridges that save nothing

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```


## `luna strict`

```text
Hardware strict mode: run a ROM and list what a real console would have refused or corrupted — a VRAM/OAM/CGRAM write or a PPU memory read while the picture is drawn (R1-R4), a DMA through the blocked A-bus zone (R5) or between WRAM and $2180 (R6), a manual joypad read during the auto-read (R8), or of `$4218-$421F` (R9), a write to `$2100` with bit 7 on the data bus (R10) or to `$2133` over a different bus byte (R11) while the picture is drawn, brightness 0 with the display on over a lit picture for a whole frame (R12, an advisory: a console shows it faintly, luna draws black). It also checks, once a frame, the sprite tiles the picture draws: a tile with pixels that no write ever filled (S1, its content is the power-on VRAM) or that was uploaded under another OBSEL layout (S4). The journal only observes: the run is identical to a plain one. One line per distinct (rule, pc, address), one per distinct (S1/S4, tile).

Exit 0 = no fault, 1 = at least one fault, 2 = the ROM cannot be loaded.

Usage: luna strict [OPTIONS] <ROM>

Arguments:
  <ROM>
          Path to the .sfc / .smc ROM file

Options:
      --frames <FRAMES>
          Number of PPU frames to run
          
          [default: 600]

      --json
          Print the report as JSON instead of text

      --force-mapper <FORCE_MAPPER>
          Force a cartridge mapper, bypassing header auto-detection. One of: lorom, hirom, exhirom, sa1, superfx, dsp1, sdd1; spc7110 is recognised but not emulated, the load refuses it

      --force-region <FORCE_REGION>
          Force the video standard (ntsc, pal)

      --power-on <POWER_ON>
          What RAM holds before the ROM boots (zero, ones, random, random=<seed>)

      --input <INPUT>
          Scripted joypad-1 input, `frame:hex` as in `state --input`: play the menus, the match, the GAME OVER under the journal

      --input2 <INPUT2>
          Scripted joypad-2 input (`state --input2` grammar)

      --input-at <INPUT_AT>
          Number the input scripts by arrivals on this routine instead of by frame (`state --input-at`; `N+K:` = K frames after arrival N)

      --poke-at <POKE_AT>
          Write every `--poke` when execution reaches this routine, at its `--poke-hit`-th arrival (`state --poke-at`). Repeatable. A poke never reached is an error (exit 2): the scenario was not played

      --poke-hit <POKE_HIT>
          With `--poke-at`: the arrival the bytes are written at (default 1)

      --poke <POKE>
          Bytes to write at the `--poke-at`: `NAME=HEX` or `BANK:OFFSET=HEX`

      --inject-nmi-at <SPEC[:N]>
          Force an NMI just BEFORE the instruction at this routine (`SPEC` or `SPEC:N`: a `.sym` label, `label+N`, or `BANK:OFFSET`; `N` = the arrival, default 1; with a bare `BANK:OFFSET` write `BANK:OFFSET:N`). A synthetic extra edge, not hardware: the real `VBlank` NMI still comes, so a frame can see two. Not injected, with the reason, when `NMITIMEN.7` is clear. Never reached: an error.
```
